pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas’s London Day Schools | Prep and Senior Schools
pageCache.text:
A family-founded group of independent schools in London which seek to give an exceptional start in life to more than 2,000 girls and boys between the ages of 3 and 18.
A Warm Welcome
Welcome to Thomas’s. We exist to ensure that our pupils achieve outstanding academic outcomes and build the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed in the world.
I have been truly impressed by the school’s breadth of opportunities offered to the children. It is clear that the school actively encourages pupils to step outside their comfort zones, try new experiences, and develop confidence in their abilities. This supportive environment helps children grow not only academically but also personally, inspiring them to challenge themselves and reach their full potential.
Ben Thomas
My family has been involved in educational leadership for more than 50 years, ever since my mother started a playgroup to keep me busy and interested when I was two years old. Over time, the playgroup became a kindergarten, the kindergarten became a prep school, the prep school became four prep schools and, with the opening of our senior school, we now offer a Thomas’s education from kindergarten to university.
A culture of joyful excellence
Our vision is that every Thomas’s pupil flourishes as a compassionate contributor to society and a courageous shaper of the future.
To realise this vision we champion kindness, community and childhood, provide a breadth of experiences that develop lifelong passions, equip young people with self-knowledge, inner strength and intellectual curiosity. Together, these commitments create the Thomas’s culture of joyful excellence.
Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Thomas’s. We invite you to visit our prep schools for a tour, make an enquiry or contact the Admissions team with any queries. We are here to support your family through every stage of our admissions process and look forward to meeting you.
Hear From Our Community
Experience the Thomas's culture of joyful excellence for yourself at one of our school tours or Open Days.
Thomas’s approach to AI in education; balancing tradition with a forward-thinking approach. How can AI be implemented thoughtfully and effectively to support our teachers and enrich pupil learning?

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Values - Thomas's London Day Schools
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
EXPLORE OUR CORE PURPOSE
Our Vision
Our vision is that every Thomas’s pupil flourishes as a compassionate contributor to society and a courageous shaper of the future.
To realise this vision, we:
Together, these commitments create the Thomas’s culture of joyful excellence, in which our pupils achieve outstanding academic outcomes and build the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed in the world.
Champion kindness, community and childhood
Our Values
Kindness centres all that we do: simply, we are kind to ourselves and we are kind to others. We are a supportive community of good friends who actively look out for one another and ensure everyone feels encouraged.
Courtesy is at the heart of how we treat others and how we act in school: we build a happier world by being unfailingly polite, considerate and mindful of the impact of our behaviour on others.
Compassion connects us all: it demands that we see the world through each other’s eyes, appreciate different perspectives, and treat everyone with care and consideration.
Scholarship sparks our curiosity: we learn to think independently, focus, and approach every new challenge with creative and critical thought and a sense of wonder.
Integrity guides our choices: it is the moral purpose that leads us to be completely honest, mean what we say, and do the right thing even when no one is watching.
Respect unites our school: we value ourselves, each other, and our environment, while proudly championing and celebrating the unique differences that make us who we are.
Perseverance turns challenges into triumphs: we cheerfully embrace hard work and patience, knowing that our minds grow stronger with effort and that setbacks are simply chances to learn.
Confidence is our quiet strength: an inner superpower, we believe in ourselves and celebrate who we are without boasting, giving us the bravery to face challenges and know that our voices truly matter.
Leadership unites courage and empathy: we lead by including everyone, taking responsibility for our actions, and use a voice that speaks up for what is right and fair for everyone.
Kindness is where we begin, and helping others is what we do: we show a true spirit of generosity by using our unique abilities, time and privileges to leave the world around us a kinder and better place.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us - Thomas's London Day Schools
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Thomas’s
Welcome to Thomas’s
My family has been involved in educational leadership for more than 50 years, ever since my mother started a playgroup to keep me busy and interested when I was 2 years old. Over time, the playgroup became a kindergarten, the kindergarten became a prep school, the prep school became four prep schools and, with the opening of our senior school, we now offer a Thomas’s education from kindergarten to university.
My mother, Joanna, had been an actress and my father, David, a soldier. As a result, my parents’ founding vision for education developed in opposition to the prevailing educational landscape in London, which they found to be more traditional, more narrow and less creative than they would have chosen for their own children. Over time, this vision crystallised around three core elements: a strong set of values, with kindness at the heart; a breadth of curriculum, full of art, dance, drama, music and sport; and academic excellence, achieved because of this approach to childhood, not in spite of it.
This vision remains at the heart of our schools and is as relevant today as it has ever been. Unless we guard against it, the UK system of entry to independent senior schools at 11 and 13 and national examinations at 16 and 18 can constrain the curriculum and have a deadening effect on our children’s education. We must serve the system in which we operate; but we must also look beyond it, to our children’s futures, to an age of machine learning and to a time when the attributes that make us uniquely human – our imagination, curiosity and creativity – will be of greater value than ever before. True to our founding history, the promise of a Thomas’s education lies in our deeply-held conviction that the best education must enable pupils to achieve outstanding academic outcomes and build the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed in the world.
For me, this is personal. For 25 years I was a Head, first at Thomas’s Kensington and then at Thomas’s Battersea and I remain incredibly proud of this distinctive style of education, which our teachers make possible for our pupils every day. My own children were pupils at Thomas’s and, as a parent, I experienced the kind, broad and strong foundations for life which they laid down and on which I see them building as young adults today.
I hope these pages convey something of the spirit of Thomas’s. If you are interested in joining us, as a pupil, a parent or a member of staff, do come and see our schools in action to gain a full understanding of the kindness, the breadth and the excellence of a Thomas’s education today. We would love to share it with you.

Governance and Leadership
THE STRATEGIC FRAMEWORK
Governance and Leadership
Our proprietor is Thomas’s London Day Schools (TLDS), a private limited company. Its shareholders are members of the Thomas family and Oakley Capital, a long-term investor since 2023.
Board of Directors
Thomas’s London Day Schools is governed on behalf of the shareholders by a Board which consists of three directors. The Board has liability and governance responsibility. It sets the strategic direction of TLDS, maintains legal oversight, monitors all activities, sets executive KPIs, assesses the performance of the schools and establishes and reviews material policies and practices governing the life of the schools.
The Board has an overriding responsibility to ensure that all safeguarding, health and safety, ISI, OFSTED and statutory obligations to our pupils, parents, staff, the Department for Education and the Education and Skills Funding Agency are met. The Board has an overriding duty to act freely and in the best interest of TLDS at all times.
Directors
Principal and Chief Executive Officer
Group Leadership Team
The Group Leadership Team is responsible for implementing the strategy set by the Board of Directors. It comprises the following senior leaders:
Principal and Chief Executive Officer
Head of Thomas’s Battersea
Head of Thomas’s Clapham
Head of Thomas’s Fulham
Head of Thomas’s Kensington
Master of Thomas’s College and Chief Education Officer
Chief Finance Officer
Chief of Staff and nominated Safeguarding Governor

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas’s Outdoors - Thomas's London Day Schools
pageCache.text:
Thomas’s Outdoors
OUTDOOR ADVENTURES AND OPPORTUNITIES
Thomas’s Daheim
We are strongly committed to outdoor education. From kindergarten onwards, we provide pupils with regular, challenging, enjoyable and safe opportunities to learn outdoors. These have a positive impact on children’s wellbeing and create shared experiences which make Thomas’s a happy and strong community.
The Thomas’s Outdoors Department is made up of outdoor education specialists, who are based within the schools and at our site at Walton Firs in Surrey. The department aims to integrate sustainability meaningfully into teaching and ensure that every child develops a strong, lasting connection with the environment.
Thomas’s Daheim (which means Thomas’s ‘At Home’) is our outdoor centre near the Kalkalpen National Park in Austria. Thomas’s has been visiting the ski area of Wurzeralm here for 40 years and has developed strong relationships and a close bond with the people and the area.
During the first half of the Lent Term, pupils in Year 5 spend a week at Thomas’s Daheim, with pupils in Year 6 returning for a week in the second half of term. The programme covers outdoor pursuits, ski lessons and a rich evening programme with the Thomas’s Outdoor vision at the heart of the children’s learning.
Our teaching staff and outdoor team lead these fabulous trips and care for our pupils, as they explore the spectacular scenery, discover ancient rock formations, study the stars in the night sky and observe local flora and fauna. Trips to Thomas’s Daheim create lifelong memories and are an unforgettable part of a Thomas’s education.

Safeguarding and Wellbeing
A COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH TO SAFEGUARDING
Safeguarding and Wellbeing
At Thomas’s, the happiness, health, and wellbeing of our entire community are central to everything we do. We believe passionately in creating an educational environment that is caring, safe, and, above all, kind. We recognise the vital importance of early intervention and provide tailored, robust support for every pupil in our schools.
Safeguarding Governance
The Proprietor (Thomas’s) has responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of children and to ensure that the Schools’ safeguarding policies, procedures and training are effective and comply with the law at all times. Pupil welfare and wellbeing extends beyond their protection from harm and neglect into areas such as promoting physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing; social and economic wellbeing; opportunities for education, training and recreation and opportunities for contributing to society.
The nominated Safeguarding Governor champions the best safeguarding practice and culture in each of the schools, supporting them to go above and beyond their statutory duties.
Our Safeguarding Teams
Each school has its own dedicated Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and a highly experienced team supporting them. If you have a concern regarding a child’s welfare, please contact the relevant team below immediately:
Designated Safeguarding Lead
batsafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
clasafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
fulsafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
kensafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
collegesafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
Understanding Safeguarding and Child Protection
While these terms are sometimes used interchangeably, we follow distinct and carefully considered approaches for each:
Safeguarding:
This is the overarching action we take to promote the welfare of all children in our care. It encompasses everything from site security and online safety to mental health support, healthy relationships education, and staff code of conduct compliance. Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility.
Child Protection:
This is a specific part of the broader safeguarding process. It focuses on protecting individual children who have been identified as suffering, or who are likely to suffer harm. It follows strict statutory child protection procedures to respond swiftly to serious concerns.
If You Have a Concern About a Child
If you believe a child is at immediate risk of harm, do not wait. Call 999 to reach the Police straight away. They will assess the situation and take immediate action to protect the child.
By raising a concern—no matter how big or how small—you could be protecting not just one child, but children in the future as well. If you are worried, always speak to a member of our safeguarding teams. If the child is not at immediate risk but you remain concerned, you can also contact your local authority’s child protection services directly.
External Resources and Support Networks
We work with local safeguarding partners, including the police, local authorities, and regional safeguarding groups to uphold the principles of the Children Act. For independent advice, parents and pupils can access the following trusted resources:
Mental Health and Wellbeing+
Helplines+

Facilities Hire
HOST YOUR NEXT EVENT WITH US
Facilities Hire at Thomas’s Battersea
28-40 Battersea High Street, London SW11 3JB
Thomas’s Battersea is located in the historic Battersea Square Conservation Area. The site consists of four main buildings (north, east, south and west) that join to form a secure central courtyard. The original east building is Grade II listed and was built in the 1800s.
The impressive grand hall, for example, is ideal for banqueting, conferences and receptions. There is additional outdoor space to the south consisting of four 3G-pitch multi-use games areas, cricket nets, a climbing wall and an adventure play area. Thomas’s Battersea has received significant investment in its facilities.
The southern wing was extended in 2012 to include a music block, the north wing was constructed in 2016 and the west wing was refurbished and extended in 2017 to provide more classrooms on the ground, first and second floors; these state-of-the-art spaces are available for a wide range of uses noted in the space hire detail below.

Join Our Team
EXPLORE CAREER OPPORTUNITIES AT THOMAS’S
Join Our Team
With more than 2000 pupils, aged 3 to18, Thomas’s London Day Schools is a dynamic and thriving group of schools. Whether you are an experienced practitioner or early in your career, you will find Thomas’s an inspiring and supportive place to work, full of possibilities and committed to educational excellence.
Thomas’s is a unique place to work. What distinguishes us is the profound sense of belonging experienced by staff. Colleagues benefit from excellent facilities, outstanding resources and a culture that is grounded in collaboration and shared purpose.
We offer the following staff benefits:
All our vacancies across the Group are listed on My New Term. We recommend creating a profile and joining our Talent Pool to receive notifications about relevant job vacancies.
Competitive salaries and pension schemes
Professional development opportunities
Generous holidays
Wellbeing services
Dining and refreshment facilities
Cycle to work scheme
A supportive and dynamic working environment
Working at Thomas’s
Members of staff at Thomas’s work as members of supportive and enthusiastic teams, across teaching and business and operations departments.
Staff across the Thomas’s group collaborate frequently with one another, exchange ideas for best practice, develop ideas and devise new ways of working.
The Thomas’s People Strategy has been created to promote a culture that reflects Thomas’s values, to develop a stimulating and motivational working environment for staff and to support the achievement of the Groups’ aims and vision.
Thomas’s is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome the unique contributions that everyone can bring to Thomas’s.
At Thomas’s we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, so we encourage you to apply even if your past experience does not align perfectly with every qualification or experience in the information provided.
Safer Recruitment and Safeguarding
Thomas’s is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Applicants will be required to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS). Full details on the checks that will be undertaken as part of our recruitment policy are detailed in our Safer Recruitment Policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Story - Thomas's London Day Schools
pageCache.text:
Our Story
DISCOVER OUR HISTORY
Our Story
David and Joanna Thomas tell their own story, and the founding story of the schools, in the documentary film below.
The existence of a kindergarten, four dynamic and interconnected independent prep schools and a selective senior school within prime London locations is the result of good luck, hard work, vision and tenacity. Initially, brought about by practical circumstances, Thomas’s was a kindergarten in a dusty church hall. Its development into the outstanding group of schools and services that it is today is the result of the Thomas family’s determined search for a broader, kinder and more creative approach to education.
Joanna Thomas, an actress, married her husband David, a Gurkha officer, in 1962. They lived in the Far East until David left the Army in 1969.
1971
Joanna was given a main part in a serial on Granada TV, which took a year to complete. In order to help juggle finances to pay for their young children’s primary education, Joanna set up a kindergarten in a local church hall in Pimlico.
1977
Six years later, the success of the kindergarten and the strong demand for London day schools of quality encouraged David Thomas to give up his job with an American bank and to join his wife in founding a school for older children. Joanna and David sold their family home, moved with their three children into a two-bedroom basement flat and, with the proceeds, took a short-term let on a building in Cadogan Gardens. After just three weeks and some intensive decorating, the first Thomas’s prep school opened its doors to eleven pupils and two teachers.
From the outset, Joanna and David were determined to create a school environment that achieved three key aims: high academic standards, an emphasis on the arts, and plenty of sport, reflecting both their personal and professional interests.
1981
In less than four years, and now known as ‘Thomas’s’, the school had more than 200 children. It expanded into two buildings in Cottesmore Gardens, just south of Kensington Gardens, to create Thomas’s Kensington.
1990
The preparatory school at Cadogan Gardens needed more space and the freehold was acquired for the former Sir Walter St John’s Grammar School in Battersea. The school, which became Thomas’s Battersea, moved to its extensive new premises and the leasehold buildings in Cadogan Gardens were sold.
1993
With an increasing demand for places, the freehold was secured for the former Clapham County Girls’ School in Broomwood Road and the new Thomas’s Clapham opened.
Thomas’s Kindergarten, Battersea was started in the crypt of St Mary’s Church educating 45 children aged from 2 to 4 years old.
1998
Thomas’s Schools Foundation (TSF) was launched at the Royal Albert Hall. The charity had two areas of focus: to identify, develop and support educational activities for children in local primary schools; and to provide funding for bursaries for children to attend a Thomas’s school.
2002
Thomas’s Kensington was provided with its own dedicated Lower School facility through the acquisition of Lady Eden’s School in Victoria Road W8. The existing buildings in Cottesmore Gardens were refurbished to become the preparatory school.
2005
Thomas’s Fulham was founded. Since 1894, this property has proudly overlooked South Park. Previously owned by the London Institute for the Chelsea College of Art and Design, located on Hugon Road, SW6. It was leased by Thomas’s in 2005 and underwent a complete refurbishment. In 2024, the lease was renewed for a further 25 years.
2007
The Principals established The CAIRN Trust as a UK registered educational charity dedicated to ensuring that children in rural Nepal are given the opportunity to gain an education.
2008
The facilities of Thomas’s Kensington were further improved through the purchase of the buildings of the Prue Leith School of Cookery in St Albans Grove W8, then converted into a purpose built theatre, a gym and a dining room.
2013
More than 1,200 Thomas’s pupils came together at The Royal Albert Hall for a spectacular performance, ‘A Celebration of Childhood’.
2015
Discussions began in response to an approach from New King’s Primary School. These led to the establishment of Thomas’s Academy, a state-funded primary school on New King’s Road. It became a member of the Thomas’s family of schools for ten years until 2025, when it joined the Quality First Education Trust.
2017
After 30 years taking school ski trips to the same small resort in Wurzeralm, Austria, Thomas’s purchased a 70-bed hotel on the mountain to create Thomas’s Daheim, now the location of week-long residential trips for pupils and an extensive outdoor learning programme.
2018
Thomas’s Schools Foundation and the CAIRN Trust merged to form Thomas’s Foundation, a charitable incorporated company which seeks to live out Thomas’s values in the world through three core projects: Foundation bursaries, community partnerships, and the CAIRN Trust.
2019
Thomas’s acquired an educational site in Putney Vale, which for four years became the home of the first Thomas’s senior school. The campus offered a broad range of high-quality facilities, including specialist Science laboratories, dedicated art and design and technology departments, and extensive provision for outdoor education and sport. The Putney Vale site has since closed, and the senior school relocated to Richmond, where it became Thomas’s College.
2021
Thomas’s took ownership of Atlantic House and Lytham House on St Albans Grove, Kensington. The buildings underwent a full refurbishment in preparation for the relocation of Thomas’s Kensington from its long-standing premises on Victoria Road and Cottesmore Gardens.
2023
Thomas’s acquired an outstanding educational site in Richmond to become the home of its senior school. The campus has a distinguished history, originally founded in 1843 as the Wesleyan Theological College. More recently, it was home to Richmond American University London. Situated on Queen’s Road, Richmond Hill, the five-acre campus is adjacent to Richmond Park.
2025
Thomas’s College opened in Richmond as a new co-educational day, flexi- and weekly-boarding school, providing a world class education for pupils aged 11 to 18, in exceptional surroundings.
Thomas’s Kensington opened the doors of its new purpose-built school in 1, St Albans Grove, W8, a landmark moment in the Thomas’s story.

Thomas’s Foundation
Thomas’s Foundation
Thomas’s Foundation, a Charitable Incorporated Organisation established in 2018, is the charitable arm of Thomas’s London Day Schools. It is driven by the belief that every child deserves an enriching education.
Thomas’s Foundation delivers its vision through two core programmes: Community Partnerships and Foundation Bursaries.
In addition, programmes supporting education in Nepal through the CAIRN Trust will continue until 2028.
Visit the Thomas’s Foundation website for further information.
Community Partnerships
Working closely with the PTA in each school, Thomas’s Foundation supports programmes that meet the greatest needs of local schoolchildren in our immediate neighbourhoods of Battersea, Clapham, Fulham, Kensington and Richmond. Through community partnerships, Thomas’s Foundation gives pupils access to inspiring and stimulating educational opportunities, which build self esteem and encourage a love of learning. More than 100 volunteers from the Thomas’s community work closely to identify, develop and manage a broad range of community partnership projects. Thomas’s Foundation funds programmes in the fields of art, drama, music, sport, outdoor learning and academic support.
Foundation Bursaries
Thomas’s Foundation funds transformational bursaries from Year 7 at Thomas’s, the amount being dependent on a family’s income, assets and circumstances. Thomas’s Foundation also helps bursary recipients with additional costs such as uniforms, books and school trips.
